directAnswer: Pope Benedict VIII (reigned 1012–1024), born Theophylact of Tusculum, was the first of three popes from the Tusculan family. He crowned Henry II emperor in 1014, worked with him on church reform, and helped repel Saracen attacks on Italy's coast.

sections.h2: The Tusculan Family Takes the Papacy
paras: Theophylact was the son of Gregory, count of Tusculum, a family descended from the circle of Theophylact and Marozia that now challenged the Crescentii for control of Rome. In 1012, after the death of Sergius IV, the Tusculans secured his election. A rival faction elected a man named Gregory, now listed as an antipope, who fled to Germany seeking King Henry II's support.
Henry backed Benedict instead, and the alliance between the pope and the German king became the foundation of Benedict's reign. With Tusculan control of Rome, the Crescentii lost their dominance.

sections.h2: Henry II's Coronation and the Creed at Mass
paras: On 14 February 1014 Benedict crowned Henry II and his wife Cunigunde in St. Peter's. According to the abbot Berno of Reichenau, who was present, Henry asked that the Creed be sung at Mass in Rome, as was customary in Germany. Benedict agreed, and the Creed, including the Filioque phrase, became part of the Roman Mass from this time.
The Filioque had been accepted in Western theology for centuries, but its liturgical use at Rome later became one of the points of dispute between the Latin and Greek churches.

Benedict took an active role in defense. In 1016 Saracen forces under Mujahid, ruler of Denia, attacked the coast near Luni and occupied parts of Sardinia. The pope organized resistance and encouraged Pisa and Genoa to take action; their fleets drove the invaders from Sardinia.

In southern Italy he supported the Lombard noble Melus of Bari against Byzantine rule, but the rebellion was defeated at Cannae in 1018. Benedict then traveled to Bamberg in 1020 to persuade Henry II to intervene, and Henry issued a privilege confirming the papal possessions. The emperor led an expedition south in 1022.

In 1022 Benedict and Henry presided over a synod at Pavia that issued decrees against clerical marriage and concubinage, forbidding priests to live with women and declaring the children of clergy to be serfs of the Church. The measures aimed primarily to prevent the loss of church property and anticipated the broader reform movement of the later eleventh century.
Benedict died on 9 April 1024 and was succeeded by his brother Romanus, who became John XIX.

keyFacts: Born Theophylact, son of Count Gregory of Tusculum
Crowned Henry II emperor on 14 February 1014
Allowed the Creed to be sung at the Roman Mass at Henry II's request
Encouraged Pisa and Genoa against Saracen forces in 1016
Presided with Henry II at the reforming Synod of Pavia (1022)

faqs.question: How did Benedict VIII change the Roman Mass?
faqs.answer: At Henry II's request in 1014, he allowed the Nicene Creed, with the Filioque, to be sung at Mass in Rome, following German practice.

faqs.question: What was Benedict VIII's relationship with Henry II?
faqs.answer: Henry supported Benedict against a rival claimant, and Benedict crowned him emperor in 1014. The two cooperated on church reform and Italian affairs.

faqs.question: What did the Synod of Pavia in 1022 decide?
faqs.answer: It forbade clerical marriage and concubinage and sought to protect church property from being passed to clergy's children.
